- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast 3–5 days post-spike at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of forecast before final output.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average of price history.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates near-term (1–7d) price movements; reduce first 7 days by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model may misread sentiment as bullish; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid false momentum.
